 American Airlines pilot declares 'mayday' after flames reportedly spotted coming from engine
 American Airlines told Fox News Digital on Friday that there was no evidence of a fire.
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Threads 
 Print 
 Email 
 Add Fox Business on Google 
 By Alex Nitzberg FOXBusiness close video Air traffic control warns American Airlines flight of flames reported from engine 
 An American Airlines flight declared "mayday" and safely returned to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport shortly after takeoff when the crew on the trailing flight warned air traffic control that they saw flames. (Courtesy: ATC.com)
 An American Airlines flight that issued a mayday call returned to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) on Thursday because of what the company has called a "mechanical issue."
 "American 3230, the SkyWest departing behind you said that they saw flames coming out of one of your engines, and you might be leaking something," air traffic control warned.
 A pilot replied that they were dealing with a "hydraulic problem" and would plan to return to the runway.
 FAA PAUSES ROUTER INSTALLATIONS NATIONWIDE AFTER TECH ISSUE CAUSED FRIDAY'S GROUND STOP 
 An American Airlines Airbus A319-112 arrives at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport from Charlotte on Jan. 22, 2025 in Arlington, Va.  (Kevin Carter/Getty Images / Getty Images) 
 When air traffic control sought confirmation that the flight wanted to return to the airport, a surprisingly calm-sounding pilot replied, "Uh, yes, mayday, mayday, mayday," and confirmed that the flight would return.
 American Airlines told Fox News Digital on Friday that there was no evidence of a fire.
 SEVERE TURBULENCE INJURES 5 ON JETBLUE FLIGHT TO FLORIDA 
 An American Airlines Airbus A319 plane, owned by the Bank of Utah Trustee, lands at Ronald Reagan National Airport (DCA) using the River Visual approach to Runway 19 on Aug. 5, 2026 in Arlington, Va.  (Al Drago/Getty Images / Getty Images) 
 The flight had been scheduled to travel from PHX to Portland International Airport (PDX), according to the company, which noted that the Airbus A319 aircraft landed safely in Phoenix.
 "American Airlines flight 3230 returned to Phoenix (PHX) due to a mechanical issue. The aircraft landed safely, taxied to the gate under its own power and was taken out of service to be inspected by our maintenance team," American Airlines said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital on Friday.
 THE ‘EXTREMELY IMPORTANT’ UNITED AIRLINES SYSTEM THAT FORCED 90-MINUTE DEPARTURE DELAY 
 An American Airlines Airbus A319 airplane taxis at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport on Nov. 7, 2026 in Arlington, Va. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images / Getty Images)

"Customers deplaned normally and re-departed on another aircraft. Safety is our top priority and we thank our team members for their professionalism and apologize to our customers for the disruption in their travel plans," the airline added.
